question: Can fewer than six IMUs support lightweight human motion reconstruction through lying, rolling and crawling using reliable contact-conditioned root estimation?
constraints: No rehabilitation templates, template matching or template-derived features
Count physically required and actually consumed sensors separately
Do not equate current local implementation with historical server runs
Do not infer contact causality from aggregate benchmark errors
Treat candidate mechanisms as untested proposals, not established novelty

claims.text: Non-foot contact, moving stationary body points and support selection already appear in TIP, PIP and GlobalPose.
Sliding and broader contact modes remain explicit limitations of several closely related methods.
Recent 2026 work narrows novelty in contact fusion, four-device physics and IMU-scene estimation.
Local benchmark results and current implementation require protocol checks before causal or sensor-efficiency conclusions.
A mode-aware contact-surface correction with calibrated reliability is a candidate requiring direct comparison against the closest prior art.
A fixed-pose oracle-contact experiment and matched causal sensor-count protocol can test whether the proposed mechanism is worthwhile.

workflow_note: Standalone literature review; no academic-pipeline passport or automated integrity certification is claimed. Two parallel read-only tasks checked original papers and repository implementation.
